plainLanguage: Georgetown builds to the 2021 International Residential Code and 2021 energy code (with city amendments), and the 2023 electrical code, effective since November 2023. Most new homes are in the RS district (minimum lot about 5,500 sq ft) or a planned development with its own setbacks - check your plat. Homes may be up to 35 ft tall. The city protects large trees: heritage trees 26 inches across or more need special care, and you usually submit a tree form with your permit. West Georgetown sits on the Edwards Aquifer recharge zone, where state (TCEQ) rules and city impervious-cover limits apply, normally handled when the subdivision was approved. The city building permit fee is roughly $125 plus 50 cents per sq ft (about $1,570 for our 2,400 sq ft example), but water, sewer and road impact fees can be much larger and were raised in 2025. The city cannot require brick, but your HOA may.
